newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-ROTOR BEAT DYNAMO, TIKHONOV BACK FOR SPARTAK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROTOR BEAT DYNAMO, TIKHONOV BACK FOR SPARTAK.

text.p: Rotor Volgograd returned to the top of the Russian league on Saturday with a convincing 3-1 victory over Dynamo Moscow, who had held the top spot for just a week.

Ominously for both, however, champions Spartak Moscow'S 2-0 win over fourth-placed Rostselmash Rostov was helped immeasurably by the surprise return from injury of winger Andrei Tikhonov, Russia's 1996 Player of the Year.

Spartak, who have won four of the five post-Soviet Russian championships, now share second place with Dynamo. After an injury-marred first third of the season, they may be back on track to retain the title and make a mark on the Champions' League.

Tikhonov, who had not played in the league since last November, came on to a roar of approval from the home crowd with 30 minutes remaining and the score locked at 0-0 against a determined Rostov side who always looked dangerous on the break.
His very presence and ability to take on defenders visibly galvanised the champions, even though Tikhonov very nearly ended up the villain of the piece.

Stepping up to take a softly-awarded penalty just 16 minutes into his first competitive match for months, he struck the post. Sergei Gorlukovich, a 35-year-old centre-back in the General Lebed mould, saved Tikhonov's blushes by heading home the rebound.
More typically, it was Tikhonov who laid on the pass to Dmitry Alenichev in the third minute of injury time to set up Andrei Konovalov for a simple header and Spartak's second.

The champions remain without their inspirational captain Ilya Tsymbalar -- he faces a knee operation in Germany this week -- and fellow midfielder Valery Kechinov. But Saturday's half-hour of Tikhonov may be the moment the 1997 championship race turned.

Dynamo, chronic under-achievers who have not won the championship since 1976, went top for the first time in two years last week and, with a Cup semifinal coming up on Tuesday against Zenit, had been tempted to turn their thoughts to a double.
Those dreams are now on hold after a convincing defeat in Volgograd. Having not conceded a goal in five matches, Dynamo let three past them for only one in reply.
Rotor, third last season, re-established their claim to take the title away from Moscow for only the second time.

In the capital derby, Lokomotiv Moscow beat Torpedo for the second time in four days, adding a 3-1 league win to their 2-1 Cup quarter-final victory. Their semifinal opponents, Krylya Sovietov Samara slumped 3-0 away to lowly KamAZ. Zenit St Petersburg, who face Dynamo in the Cup, went down 2-0 to CSKA in Moscow.
Elsewhere, the nightmare continued for 1995 champions Alania Vladikavkaz. Last year's runners-up were held to a scoreless draw at home by second-bottom Tyumen and remain anchored in mid-table.
